title: Almond milk vs. oat milk: nutrition differences

seo.title: Almond milk vs. oat milk: calories, protein and calcium
seo.meta_description: Compare current unsweetened almond and oat milks per cup for calories, protein, carbs, calcium and vitamin D.
seo.search_intent: Compare almond milk and oat milk nutrition

excerpt: In current unsweetened examples, Silk almond milk has 30 calories and 1 g protein per cup; Oatly Unsweetened has 40 calories and 0 g. Much of the calcium comes from fortification.
content_html:
Almond and oat milk can look interchangeable in coffee, but their labels differ. Both examples here are unsweetened.

One cup

Silk Unsweet AlmondOatly Unsweetened
Calories3040
Protein1 g0 g
Fat3 g1.5 g
Carbohydrate1 g6 g
Calcium470 mg320 mg
Vitamin D4 mcg4 mcg

Both are low in protein

Neither is a meaningful protein replacement for dairy or soy milk.

Oat milk carries more carbohydrate

The oat example has 6 g per cup versus 1 g in almond milk.

Calcium comes largely from fortification

Manufacturers add calcium and vitamin D, so formulas vary.

Which is better?

Unsweetened almond milk fits very-low-calorie goals; oat milk offers different flavor and body. For protein, look elsewhere or choose a higher-protein formula.
